what: A capture gate that ran its 50 steps and was then killed while writing the captured frames: instratus_condensate answered by the original at its hook with every call's frame recorded, 9000 calls per rank.
outcome: model run exited 137 (rank 1 killed by signal 9, the rest by SIGTERM) during _save_frame_captures; all 512 npz files truncated; no summary, no capture.json
bfb_record_note: pi_cam_pausable_instratus-capture_vs_oracle_50step_bfb.json was written by the job's comparison of the history the run had finished before it died; it is not evidence of a capture, and the resubmitted gate reuses the name.
diagnosis: Memory, not numerics: resources_used.mem reached exactly the job's 256 GB request and the out-of-memory killer took one rank.  This kernel is called 9000 times per rank in 50 steps and its frame is 29 small arrays, so the capture holds about a quarter of a million NumPy objects per rank -- far more per-object overhead than the micro_mg_tend capture (100 large frames per rank) that fit the same request.  The hook gate without capture (7371011) ran at the same request and passed.
disposition: Resubmit the capture gate with 235 GB per node and a 30-minute walltime; consider a lighter capture layout (one contiguous array per argument) for high-frequency kernels.
